hypotheses.justification: hM is only passed to meanClass_dividedAlias, which only passes it to dividedAlias_global_bounds. There it is used once, as the `M ≠ 0` argument of UniformFourierAlias.real_exactAlias_finiteJets with p = 0. That call yields a bound KA*B with no |M|⁻¹ gain, so M ≠ 0 buys nothing. The same bound holds for every M, including M = 0. exactAlias χ M v G = deriv χ y.1 • totalIntegral M v G y, where totalIntegral M v f z = ∫ u, f (shift M v z u). TransportPrimitive.iteratedFDeriv_totalIntegral_norm_le (TransportPrimitive.lean:1014, no condition on M) gives ‖iteratedFDeriv n (totalIntegral M v G) z‖ ≤ B*(b^d-a^d), using the source bound hsource, which holds at every point (Set.univ). RadialPullback.radial_multiplier_finiteJets_uniform with h = deriv χ (smooth) gives the multiplier bound K*C, uniform in F, for z.1 ∈ Icc (a^d) (b^d). Outside that interval the jet vanishes by UniformFourierAlias.exactAlias_supported plus TransportPrimitive.iteratedFDeriv_supported. This is the argument of the downstream lemma exactAlias_bounded_fiber (LocalSignedRequest.lean:1445), which has no M ≠ 0 hypothesis; that file imports TemporalMeanUpdate, so its proof must be copied, but every ingredient is upstream. So replace hbA in dividedAlias_global_bounds by this M-free bound, with constant K*B*(b^d-a^d), uniform in n. The other steps of meanClass_dividedAlias (physicalAlias_contDiff, physicalAlias_supported, the interior support lemma, meanClass_of_interior_bounds, dividedAlias_finiteJets_transfer) already hold for arbitrary M. So the conclusion holds and is provable without hM, including when some M n = 0.
